In this work, we present an updated catalogue of 1,047 calibration sources in the ALMACAL−22 sample, including new redshifts obtained from recent Very Large Telescope (VLT) observations (Section 2).

We examine the redshift properties of the calibrators, as well as their infrared classifications based on WISE data (Section 3). Finally, we re-evaluate the radio spectral energy distributions of the calibrators (Section 4)

The SED is fitted using four analytical models: i) a power law for steep, flat, or inverted spectra, ii) a simple peaked spectrum source model (Snellen et al. 1998), iii) a peaked spectrum model with curvature (Orienti et al. 2007) and iv) a re-triggered source modelled by a linear combination of the power law and simple peaked spectrum source models.
We also include an approximation of the linear source size on the secondary 𝑦-axis using a scaling relation (Jeyakumar 2016).

We also introduce a final class labelled ‘complex’ to describe data that is poorly-fitted, has unusual model parameters or unnatural spectral indices.

To fully exploit the ALMACAL data, understanding the properties of the calibrators is crucial. For instance, obtaining accurate redshifts is necessary to ensure that the calibrator is at a higher redshift than foreground galaxies in stacking experiments (Klitsch et al. 2023).

Moreover, verifying that CO emitters are at different redshifts from the calibrators is important to ensure that measured CO luminosity functions are not affected by clustering (Hamanowicz et al. 2023; Chen et al. 2023b).
